risks.risk: Panel specifications (wattage per panel, brand, model) are not readable, so the true value cannot be priced accurately.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the panel label/serial plate showing brand, model, and rated wattage (W), plus Voc/Isc.
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic used solar panels with unknown wattage (worst-case: lower output/older specs).

risks.risk: Unclear whether panels are new or used, and whether they are fully functional (degradation, cracks, water ingress).
risks.proof: A short video/clip showing each panel’s junction box area and a multimeter/IV test report (or at least a working test screenshot) for output.
risks.if_unproven: Price as used and not guaranteed (worst-case: treat as not tested/possibly underperforming).

risks.risk: Unclear if the sale includes only panels or also inverter/charge controller/cables/mounting hardware.
risks.proof: A photo of the full package contents laid out (inverter, charge controller, batteries if any, cables, mounting rails, fuses/MC4s) and a written itemized list.
risks.if_unproven: Price as panels only (worst-case: exclude any inverter/charge controller value).

risks.risk: Quantity and configuration are uncertain (how many panels total, and whether they are wired in series/parallel).
risks.proof: A wide shot showing the entire array and a close-up of the wiring/combiner/junction box showing series/parallel connections.
risks.if_unproven: Price for the visible portion only and assume wiring/config is unknown (worst-case: value reduced).

proof_requests: Clear close-up of each panel’s label/serial plate (brand, model, rated wattage, Voc/Isc).
Photo/video of junction boxes and wiring/MC4 connectors (showing condition and how they’re connected).
A photo of the full items included in the deal (confirm whether inverter/charge controller are included or not).
A test proof: IV curve/test report or a working output measurement under sun (or a technician test screenshot).
response.reason: The photo shows a solar panel array, but the key pricing drivers (panel brand/model/wattage, quantity, and whether it’s tested/working) are not readable or verifiable from the single image. Without those, any price would be guesswork.
